<div class="callout-note">
<h2>Help us create the best guidance possible</h2>
<p>If you would like anything added to or clarified in this guidance, email the Identification Management team at <a href="mailto:idmstandards@gdda.govt.nz">idmstandards@gdda.govt.nz</a>.</p>
</div>
<h2>Introduction</h2>
<p>Within Identification Management, pieces of information (or attributes) have values. For example, ‘<time datetime="2023-10-01">01/10/2023</time>’ is a date value and ‘blue’ is a colour value.</p>
<p>Most of the time these values are authoritative values or copies of authoritative values. This is the most common method of establishing values, but there are other methods.</p>
<p>This guidance describes:</p>
<ul>
<li>the methods used to establish values and where these values fit within the levels of information assurance</li>
<li>the concepts of low and zero-knowledge proofs when information is presented.</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/standards-and-guidance/identity/identification-management/identification-terminology">Identification terminology — definitions of key terms used on this page</a></p>
<p>This content is part of the wider Identification Standards and will evolve and expand over time to meet the needs of readers.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/standards-and-guidance/identification-standards">Identification Standards</a></p>
<h2>Methods of establishing values</h2>
<p>There are 4 main ways to establish values. Each is described here.</p>
<div class="accordion-toggle inline-accordion">
<div class="accordion-trigger">
<span class="accordion-title">
<button type="button" class="accordion-toggle__btn" lang="en-NZ" hidden="">Expand all
</button>
</span>
</div>
</div>


<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Establishing an authoritative value" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Establishing an authoritative value</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>An authoritative value is established or created by the authority for the information.</p>
<p>The value is deemed to be accurate regardless of the method or process the authority uses to establish the value.</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<h4>Examples of authoritative values</h4>
<ul>
<li>An Entity saying their favourite colour is ‘blue’.</li>
<li>Date of birth established by the registrar of births.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>



<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Establishing a derived value" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Establishing a derived value</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>A value is derived when it is directly calculated from one or more values.</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<h4>Examples of derived values</h4>
<ul>
<li>The initials <abbr>JPG</abbr> are derived from the name John Paul Getty.</li>
<li>An Entity’s age is derived from its date of creation or birth and another point in time, such as today.</li>
<li>A suburb is derived from its postal code.</li>
<li>An Entity saying their age is ‘32’.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>



<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Establishing an inferred value" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Establishing an inferred value</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>An inferred (or deduced) value takes 1 or more pieces of information and makes an assumption. As many other things could influence the assumption, these values are more subjective and less certain.</p>
<p>Often inferred values are not directly related to the value (or values), that’s being used for the assumption.</p>
<p>While using more points of reference can increase the likelihood of the value being accurate, it cannot be assumed that it is accurate. This impacts the Level of Information Assurance (<abbr>LoIA</abbr>).</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<h4>Examples of inferred values</h4>
<ul>
<li>A person wears lots of blue clothing so blue is their favourite colour.</li>
<li>A person has a credit card so they’re over 18 years old.</li>
<li>A person needs to be 18 years old to be enrolled to vote, so people on the electoral role are at least 18 years old.</li>
<li>A person works and shops in a place, so this is where they live.</li>
<li>Aggregating an Entity’s social media posts and then making assumptions about their political views, their age, or their preference for cats over dogs.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>



<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Establishing an estimated value" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Establishing an estimated value</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>A value is deemed to be estimated if it is established using statistical analysis.</p>
<p>An estimated value may come from large sets of information such as financial, biometric (physical or behavioural) or locational.</p>
<p>Estimations using biometric information have the benefit of also being bound to the Entity that’s the subject of the estimation.</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<h4>Examples of estimated values</h4>
<ul>
<li>By analysing a facial image against known parameters, it’s estimated that this person is aged 40 or between 35 and 45 years old.</li>
<li>After analysing voice recordings against known parameters, it’s estimated that this person is in a bad mood or comes from a particular region.</li>
<li>By analysing financial transactions on spending, it’s estimated an Entity’s salary is $50,000 per year.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>

<div class="callout-note callout--no-title" role="note">
<p>Information Privacy Principles are to be applied to all information collected or generated.</p>
</div>
<h2>How values are expressed</h2>
<p>A large portion of the information used in identification management uses formatting standards, such as for dates, account numbers and addresses.</p>
<p>Most values are expressed as ordinary alpha or numeric values. However, some are both alpha and numeric.</p>
<p>Values can also be expressed in the following ways.</p>
<div class="accordion-toggle inline-accordion">
<div class="accordion-trigger">
<span class="accordion-title">
<button type="button" class="accordion-toggle__btn" lang="en-NZ" hidden="">Expand all
</button>
</span>
</div>
</div>


<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Ranges" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Ranges</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>Values can be expressed as a range such as between x and y or greater than x and less than y. This can include statements like under or over. For example, the Entity is under 65 years of age or over 18 years of age.</p>
</div>
</details>



<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Binary response" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Binary response</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>If a request for information comes as a closed question about the value of a piece of information or attribute, then the value of the response can be expressed in binary forms such as:</p>
<ul>
<li>1 or 0</li>
<li>Yes or No</li>
<li>green tick or red cross.</li>
</ul>
<p>Some responses might allow for the addition of values (such as other, exception or maybe), which can invite the Relying Party to take other actions that are specific to the context.</p>
</div>
</details>



<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Codes" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Codes</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>A value can be replaced by a code to:</p>
<ul>
<li>save system storage space</li>
<li>reduce the size of information sharing files</li>
<li>obscure a value from being read by unauthorised parties.</li>
</ul>
<div class="callout-example">
<h4>Examples of where codes are commonly used</h4>
<ul>
<li>the names of countries expressed as 2 or 3 letter country codes for which there are international standards.</li>
<li>codes for airports in the aviation industry.</li>
<li>codes to represent gender.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p>Whenever codes are used to reduce information, the Relying Party will need to have access to data which decodes the values. This data could be public or private.</p>
</div>
</details>

<h2>Applying levels of information assurance</h2>
<p>The method used to establish a value impacts the level of assurance that can be achieved by the value.</p>
<div class="callout-note callout--no-title" role="note">
<p>The level of information assurance is only an indicator of the accuracy of a value. Entity binding is still needed to ensure the value relates to the Entity that’s claiming it.</p>
</div>
<div class="accordion-toggle inline-accordion">
<div class="accordion-trigger">
<span class="accordion-title">
<button type="button" class="accordion-toggle__btn" lang="en-NZ" hidden="">Expand all
</button>
</span>
</div>
</div>


<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Authoritative and derived values" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Authoritative and derived values</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>The level of information assurance for these reflect the:</p>
<ul>
<li>value’s distance from the authoritative source</li>
<li>quality of the evidence used to verify the value.</li>
</ul>
<p>The controls for levels of information assurance are contained in the Information Assurance Standard.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/standards-and-guidance/identification-standards/information-assurance-standard">Information Assurance Standard</a></p>
<p>A derived value calculated from an authoritative value inherits the assurance level of the authoritative value. However, when the Relying Party stores a value, it becomes a copy and drops down a level of assurance.</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<h4>Examples of derived value assurance levels</h4>
<ul>
<li>If a date of birth is known to be <abbr>LoIA</abbr>3, then an age derived from this date of birth is also <abbr>LoIA3</abbr>.</li>
<li>If total income of ‘$31,576.23’ is known to be <abbr>LoIA2</abbr>, then an income range of between $30k and $35k derived from that, will also be <abbr>LoIA2</abbr>.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>



<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Inferred values" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Inferred values</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>Inferred values, like derived values, inherit the <abbr>LoIA</abbr> of the information that’s used for the inference. But this is only if there are no exceptions or conditions associated with the information from which it was inferred.</p>
<p>When there are exceptions or conditions that could impact the assumption, the lowest level of information assurance (<abbr>LoIA1</abbr>) is used.</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<h4>Examples of inferred value assurance levels</h4>
<ul>
<li>Where marriage is only permitted between individuals over the age of 16, a valid government-issued marriage certificate containing name information at <abbr>LoIA3</abbr>, would infer that the named individuals are over 16 to <abbr>LoIA3</abbr>.</li>
<li>Regardless of the <abbr>LoIA</abbr> of the information about where a person works and shops, they could live at a different location. So, the inference that they live at the same location as where they work and shop will be at <abbr>LoIA1</abbr>.</li>
<li>A person’s decision to wear blue maybe influenced by an employment policy rather than their personal choice, so inferring blue is their favourite colour will be at <abbr>LoIA1</abbr>.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>



<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Estimated values" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Estimated values</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>In general, estimated values should be considered as <abbr>LoIA1</abbr> for accuracy. This is because even those using authoritative information or attributes, are based on probabilistic prediction.</p>
<p>Estimated value results will always include false positives and false negatives.</p>
<p>There are some situations where a Relying Party can have more trust in an estimated value and accept it as <abbr>LoIA2</abbr>.</p>
<p>However, the added situations will not be sufficient for an estimated value to be considered as equal to an authoritative source or to a direct copy it.</p>
<p>A Relying Party will need to implement additional risk mitigations where the risk indicates that a higher level of assurance is needed.</p>
<p>Situations that may increase trust in an estimated value:</p>
<ul>
<li>the information source on which the estimate is based</li>
<li>the method of estimation used</li>
<li>whether the estimation is expressed precisely or as a range, thereby allowing for margins of error</li>
<li>if the information used for the estimation has no uncounted or uncontrollable factors that could impact the result. For instance, if a facial expression in an image cannot be controlled it could impact the result, such as smiling reducing an age estimate</li>
<li>whether the method of estimation has empirical evidence of its efficacy.</li>
</ul>
<div class="callout-example">
<h4>Examples of estimated value assurance levels</h4>
<ul>
<li>Estimation of a facial image using an unknown method and source to be 40 years old, <abbr>LoIA1</abbr>.</li>
<li>Estimation of a facial image of the live Entity using a reliable verified method to be between 35 and 45 years old, <abbr>LoIA2</abbr>.</li>
<li>Analysing voice recordings to estimate mood and region would likely have too many uncounted and uncontrollable factors to be more than <abbr>LoIA1</abbr>.</li>
<li>An analysis of spending does not account for whether the person spends all their money or saves some, so an estimated salary of $50,000 per year is <abbr>LoIA1</abbr>.</li>
<li>An analysis of spending does not account for the source of income, so an estimated salary of more than $50,000 per year would still need to be taken as <abbr>LoIA1</abbr>.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>

<h2>Presentation of information</h2>
<p>The following guidance is for Credential and Facilitation Providers who provide values on which others rely, that are derived, inferred or estimated.</p>
<h3>Meta data about how the value was created</h3>
<p>A Credential or Facilitation Provider must advise the Relying Party when the information given has been derived, inferred or estimated.</p>
<p>Additional information about the value that can be made available to the Relying Party includes:</p>
<ul>
<li>the method used to establish the value — derived, inferred or estimated</li>
<li>the <abbr>LoIA</abbr>&nbsp;or source of information used to arrive at the value</li>
<li>how this information was used to create the value, especially if it’s an estimate</li>
<li>for inferred and estimated values — a description of the level and nature of the testing done to ensure the efficacy of the results generated by the method.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Low and zero-knowledge proofs</h3>
<p>Low and zero-knowledge proofs describe situations where the Facilitation Provider can make available information without disclosing the original value.</p>
<p>The Relying Party requests information about the value rather than requesting the value itself.</p>
<div class="accordion-toggle inline-accordion">
<div class="accordion-trigger">
<span class="accordion-title">
<button type="button" class="accordion-toggle__btn" lang="en-NZ" hidden="">Expand all
</button>
</span>
</div>
</div>


<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h4">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Low-knowledge proofs" data-ga-label="/home">
<h4>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Low-knowledge proofs</span>




</h4>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>Low-knowledge proofs obscure the precise value by either placing it within a larger number of values or expressing it in a more general way.</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<h5>Examples of low-knowledge proofs</h5>
<ul>
<li>Making available an age instead of the date of birth.</li>
<li>Expressing a date of birth as within a range of dates.</li>
<li>Providing a maximum or minimum date, that’s not the date itself.</li>
<li>Expressing salary as within a range — the bigger the range the lower the knowledge.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>



<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h4">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Zero-knowledge proofs" data-ga-label="/home">
<h4>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Zero-knowledge proofs</span>




</h4>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>Zero-knowledge proofs make use of binary responses. Rather than asking for an attribute, the Relying Party provides the Facilitation Provider with a distinct set of parameters that the value of the attribute needs to meet.</p>
<p>The Facilitation Provider applies the parameters to what they know and provides a binary response — which could include indicating they’re unable to respond.</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<h5>Examples of zero-knowledge proof questions and responses</h5>
<ul>
<li>Is this Entity over 18 years of age? Yes.</li>
<li>Is this Entity living in New Zealand? Yes.</li>
<li>Is this Entity a permanent resident? Green tick.</li>
<li>Does this Entity meet the criteria (this would be defined) for this service? Red cross.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>

<h2>Related advice</h2>
<p>The following resources are related to this topic:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/standards-and-guidance/identification-standards/information-assurance-standard">Information Assurance Standard</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/standards-and-guidance/identification-standards/implementing-the-information-assurance-standard">Implementing the Information Assurance Standard</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Contact</h2>
<p>Government Digital Delivery Agency<br>Email: <a href="mailto:idmstandards@gdda.govt.nz">idmstandards@gdda.govt.nz</a></p>

<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>A value is deemed to be estimated if it is established using statistical analysis.</p>
<p>An estimated value may come from large sets of information such as financial, biometric (physical or behavioural) or locational.</p>
<p>Estimations using biometric information have the benefit of also being bound to the Entity that’s the subject of the estimation.</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<h4>Examples of estimated values</h4>
<ul>
<li>By analysing a facial image against known parameters, it’s estimated that this person is aged 40 or between 35 and 45 years old.</li>
<li>After analysing voice recordings against known parameters, it’s estimated that this person is in a bad mood or comes from a particular region.</li>
<li>By analysing financial transactions on spending, it’s estimated an Entity’s salary is $50,000 per year.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>

<div class="callout-note callout--no-title" role="note">
<p>Information Privacy Principles are to be applied to all information collected or generated.</p>
</div>
<h2>How values are expressed</h2>
<p>A large portion of the information used in identification management uses formatting standards, such as for dates, account numbers and addresses.</p>
<p>Most values are expressed as ordinary alpha or numeric values. However, some are both alpha and numeric.</p>
<p>Values can also be expressed in the following ways.</p>
<div class="accordion-toggle inline-accordion">
<div class="accordion-trigger">
<span class="accordion-title">
<button type="button" class="accordion-toggle__btn" lang="en-NZ" hidden="">Expand all
</button>
</span>
</div>
</div>


<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Ranges" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Ranges</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>Values can be expressed as a range such as between x and y or greater than x and less than y. This can include statements like under or over. For example, the Entity is under 65 years of age or over 18 years of age.</p>
</div>
</details>



<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Binary response" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Binary response</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>If a request for information comes as a closed question about the value of a piece of information or attribute, then the value of the response can be expressed in binary forms such as:</p>
<ul>
<li>1 or 0</li>
<li>Yes or No</li>
<li>green tick or red cross.</li>
</ul>
<p>Some responses might allow for the addition of values (such as other, exception or maybe), which can invite the Relying Party to take other actions that are specific to the context.</p>
</div>
</details>



<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Codes" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Codes</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>A value can be replaced by a code to:</p>
<ul>
<li>save system storage space</li>
<li>reduce the size of information sharing files</li>
<li>obscure a value from being read by unauthorised parties.</li>
</ul>
<div class="callout-example">
<h4>Examples of where codes are commonly used</h4>
<ul>
<li>the names of countries expressed as 2 or 3 letter country codes for which there are international standards.</li>
<li>codes for airports in the aviation industry.</li>
<li>codes to represent gender.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p>Whenever codes are used to reduce information, the Relying Party will need to have access to data which decodes the values. This data could be public or private.</p>
</div>
</details>

<h2>Applying levels of information assurance</h2>
<p>The method used to establish a value impacts the level of assurance that can be achieved by the value.</p>
<div class="callout-note callout--no-title" role="note">
<p>The level of information assurance is only an indicator of the accuracy of a value. Entity binding is still needed to ensure the value relates to the Entity that’s claiming it.</p>
</div>
<div class="accordion-toggle inline-accordion">
<div class="accordion-trigger">
<span class="accordion-title">
<button type="button" class="accordion-toggle__btn" lang="en-NZ" hidden="">Expand all
</button>
</span>
</div>
</div>


<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Authoritative and derived values" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Authoritative and derived values</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>The level of information assurance for these reflect the:</p>
<ul>
<li>value’s distance from the authoritative source</li>
<li>quality of the evidence used to verify the value.</li>
</ul>
<p>The controls for levels of information assurance are contained in the Information Assurance Standard.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/standards-and-guidance/identification-standards/information-assurance-standard">Information Assurance Standard</a></p>
<p>A derived value calculated from an authoritative value inherits the assurance level of the authoritative value. However, when the Relying Party stores a value, it becomes a copy and drops down a level of assurance.</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<h4>Examples of derived value assurance levels</h4>
<ul>
<li>If a date of birth is known to be <abbr>LoIA</abbr>3, then an age derived from this date of birth is also <abbr>LoIA3</abbr>.</li>
<li>If total income of ‘$31,576.23’ is known to be <abbr>LoIA2</abbr>, then an income range of between $30k and $35k derived from that, will also be <abbr>LoIA2</abbr>.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>



<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Inferred values" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Inferred values</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>Inferred values, like derived values, inherit the <abbr>LoIA</abbr> of the information that’s used for the inference. But this is only if there are no exceptions or conditions associated with the information from which it was inferred.</p>
<p>When there are exceptions or conditions that could impact the assumption, the lowest level of information assurance (<abbr>LoIA1</abbr>) is used.</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<h4>Examples of inferred value assurance levels</h4>
<ul>
<li>Where marriage is only permitted between individuals over the age of 16, a valid government-issued marriage certificate containing name information at <abbr>LoIA3</abbr>, would infer that the named individuals are over 16 to <abbr>LoIA3</abbr>.</li>
<li>Regardless of the <abbr>LoIA</abbr> of the information about where a person works and shops, they could live at a different location. So, the inference that they live at the same location as where they work and shop will be at <abbr>LoIA1</abbr>.</li>
<li>A person’s decision to wear blue maybe influenced by an employment policy rather than their personal choice, so inferring blue is their favourite colour will be at <abbr>LoIA1</abbr>.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>



<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h3">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Estimated values" data-ga-label="/home">
<h3>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Estimated values</span>




</h3>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>In general, estimated values should be considered as <abbr>LoIA1</abbr> for accuracy. This is because even those using authoritative information or attributes, are based on probabilistic prediction.</p>
<p>Estimated value results will always include false positives and false negatives.</p>
<p>There are some situations where a Relying Party can have more trust in an estimated value and accept it as <abbr>LoIA2</abbr>.</p>
<p>However, the added situations will not be sufficient for an estimated value to be considered as equal to an authoritative source or to a direct copy it.</p>
<p>A Relying Party will need to implement additional risk mitigations where the risk indicates that a higher level of assurance is needed.</p>
<p>Situations that may increase trust in an estimated value:</p>
<ul>
<li>the information source on which the estimate is based</li>
<li>the method of estimation used</li>
<li>whether the estimation is expressed precisely or as a range, thereby allowing for margins of error</li>
<li>if the information used for the estimation has no uncounted or uncontrollable factors that could impact the result. For instance, if a facial expression in an image cannot be controlled it could impact the result, such as smiling reducing an age estimate</li>
<li>whether the method of estimation has empirical evidence of its efficacy.</li>
</ul>
<div class="callout-example">
<h4>Examples of estimated value assurance levels</h4>
<ul>
<li>Estimation of a facial image using an unknown method and source to be 40 years old, <abbr>LoIA1</abbr>.</li>
<li>Estimation of a facial image of the live Entity using a reliable verified method to be between 35 and 45 years old, <abbr>LoIA2</abbr>.</li>
<li>Analysing voice recordings to estimate mood and region would likely have too many uncounted and uncontrollable factors to be more than <abbr>LoIA1</abbr>.</li>
<li>An analysis of spending does not account for whether the person spends all their money or saves some, so an estimated salary of $50,000 per year is <abbr>LoIA1</abbr>.</li>
<li>An analysis of spending does not account for the source of income, so an estimated salary of more than $50,000 per year would still need to be taken as <abbr>LoIA1</abbr>.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>

<h2>Presentation of information</h2>
<p>The following guidance is for Credential and Facilitation Providers who provide values on which others rely, that are derived, inferred or estimated.</p>
<h3>Meta data about how the value was created</h3>
<p>A Credential or Facilitation Provider must advise the Relying Party when the information given has been derived, inferred or estimated.</p>
<p>Additional information about the value that can be made available to the Relying Party includes:</p>
<ul>
<li>the method used to establish the value — derived, inferred or estimated</li>
<li>the <abbr>LoIA</abbr>&nbsp;or source of information used to arrive at the value</li>
<li>how this information was used to create the value, especially if it’s an estimate</li>
<li>for inferred and estimated values — a description of the level and nature of the testing done to ensure the efficacy of the results generated by the method.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Low and zero-knowledge proofs</h3>
<p>Low and zero-knowledge proofs describe situations where the Facilitation Provider can make available information without disclosing the original value.</p>
<p>The Relying Party requests information about the value rather than requesting the value itself.</p>
<div class="accordion-toggle inline-accordion">
<div class="accordion-trigger">
<span class="accordion-title">
<button type="button" class="accordion-toggle__btn" lang="en-NZ" hidden="">Expand all
</button>
</span>
</div>
</div>


<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h4">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Low-knowledge proofs" data-ga-label="/home">
<h4>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Low-knowledge proofs</span>




</h4>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>Low-knowledge proofs obscure the precise value by either placing it within a larger number of values or expressing it in a more general way.</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<h5>Examples of low-knowledge proofs</h5>
<ul>
<li>Making available an age instead of the date of birth.</li>
<li>Expressing a date of birth as within a range of dates.</li>
<li>Providing a maximum or minimum date, that’s not the date itself.</li>
<li>Expressing salary as within a range — the bigger the range the lower the knowledge.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>



<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h4">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="Zero-knowledge proofs" data-ga-label="/home">
<h4>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">Zero-knowledge proofs</span>




</h4>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>Zero-knowledge proofs make use of binary responses. Rather than asking for an attribute, the Relying Party provides the Facilitation Provider with a distinct set of parameters that the value of the attribute needs to meet.</p>
<p>The Facilitation Provider applies the parameters to what they know and provides a binary response — which could include indicating they’re unable to respond.</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<h5>Examples of zero-knowledge proof questions and responses</h5>
<ul>
<li>Is this Entity over 18 years of age? Yes.</li>
<li>Is this Entity living in New Zealand? Yes.</li>
<li>Is this Entity a permanent resident? Green tick.</li>
<li>Does this Entity meet the criteria (this would be defined) for this service? Red cross.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</details>

<h2>Related advice</h2>
<p>The following resources are related to this topic:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/standards-and-guidance/identification-standards/information-assurance-standard">Information Assurance Standard</a></li>
<li><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/standards-and-guidance/identification-standards/implementing-the-information-assurance-standard">Implementing the Information Assurance Standard</a>.</li>
</ul>

<p>Government Digital Delivery Agency<br>Email: <a href="mailto:idmstandards@gdda.govt.nz">idmstandards@gdda.govt.nz</a></p>
